To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the latent representations of a complex system are more disentangled when trained on multimodal data than on a single modality; and (ii) the representations are better suited for further tasks such a model-based RL, if they are learned with the objective to be disentangled

(1) the latent space of the VAE is a good representation for the task of predicting future states and (2) the VAE is able to disentangle most of the relevant factors of variation, but it is unable to disentangle the factors of variation that are not directly visible in the images

1) the dataset and evaluation framework are useful for the research community to evaluate and compare representation learning algorithms; 2) the representation learning algorithms are not able to learn a good latent representation of the data; 3) the disentanglement score is useful to evaluate the quality of the representation learning algorithms, and; 4) the representation learning algorithm based on variational auto-encoders performs best on the dataset

we provide a large-scale benchmark dataset for representation learning in the context of landing an airplane, and we provide a set of baselines to compare future approaches to representation learning.

the latent representations learned by the proposed methods can be used to improve performance in downstream tasks, such as supervised learning tasks, model-based reinforcement tasks and anomaly detection tasks, compared to the original raw input data.

the latent representation of a complex system can be learned from multiple modalities, which can then be used to solve a variety of downstream tasks.
the quality of learned representations depends on the choice of the training objective, and that a combination of multiple objectives leads to the best results.
